conviction_note: The baseline carries history.n=0, so I rebuilt the reaction base rate from Yahoo daily bars: print-day close to next-session close was -0.92% (13 Feb 25), -6.80% (20 May 25), +3.06% (18 Aug 25), -7.42% (19 Nov 25), -6.82% (17 Feb 26), -5.63% (2 Jun 26), and +7.19% (19 Aug 24) - median |move| 6.8% against a 7.77% implied, so the straddle is fair-to-slightly-rich, and mean signed -2.5%. Crucially the two fiscal-year-end August prints (+7.19%, +3.06%) are the ONLY positives in seven, which is the most relevant subsample for tonight and which agrees with the -17.1 calls-bid skew, so I treat the reaction history as PRICED rather than as an edge. My -1.5 is the residual after netting three specific negatives (FY27 EPS denominator, live deal-announcement risk, federal price realisation) against that seasonal, against blowout peer prints (CRWD record net-new ARR, FTNT product +52%, OKTA +20%), and against the ~4 points of PANW-specific de-risking already taken today (PANW -5.2% intraday vs Nasdaq -1.4%).

findings.finding: The market paid +12.84% in one session (close 339.31 on 26 Aug to 382.85 on 27 Aug 2026) for nothing but a StreetInsider rumour that PANW is circling Cribl ($3.5bn) and ClickHouse ($15bn) - yet every time PANW has actually announced a deal the stock has been sold: -14% over two days on the CyberArk announcement (30 Jul 2025) and -7.42% the session after the 19 Nov 2025 print at which Chronosphere was announced alongside a double beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has the rumour in it as a POSITIVE and has it the wrong way round. If the market had priced PANW's own deal-announcement reaction function, the 25-delta skew would not be -17.1 vol points with calls bid into a print at which this management has previously announced a multi-billion acquisition (Chronosphere, on the Q1 FY26 call); you would see puts bid ahead of a live, named, rumoured deal. Instead upside is the expensive side, so the tail that PANW confirms a Cribl/ClickHouse-scale deal tonight is effectively unhedged. Note also that the rumour pop is being unwound rather than confirmed - PANW is -5.2% intraday today against a Nasdaq -1.4%.
findings.independence: Independent confirmation of the -14% CyberArk-announcement reaction from Forbes, 2025-07-30: https://www.forbes.com/sites/petercohan/2025/07/30/palo-alto-networks-stock-down-14-on-dubious-25-billion-cyberark-buy/ . Independent confirmation that Chronosphere was announced ON the 19 Nov 2025 earnings call from SiliconANGLE, 2025-11-19: https://siliconangle.com/2025/11/19/palo-alto-networks-announces-3-35b-chronosphere-acquisition-beating-earnings-forecast/ . SOURCE-CLUSTER NOTE: the -7.42% and +12.84% figures are both computed from the same Yahoo daily-bar series I also use in finding 2 - https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PANW?period1=1787270400&period2=1788307200&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PANW?period1=1763424000&period2=1763942400&interval=1d - so treat the price series as one document across findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: Tonight's first-ever FY27 EPS guide has to be built on roughly 9-10% more shares than the FY26 base: PANW's own Q3 FY26 release guides FY26 diluted shares to 763-766m but Q4 alone to 830-840m, and PANW has already cut its own FY26 EPS guide once on this exact mechanism (from $3.80-3.90 to $3.65-3.70 on 17 Feb 2026, on deal costs that more than doubled), a print after which the stock closed -6.82%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 number cannot surprise: published consensus IS the company's guide (Q4 revenue $3,352m vs guide $3,345-3,355m; EPS $0.97 vs guide $0.96-0.98; shares 830-840m identical to the guide). So the only unanchored number tonight is the FY27 guide, and it is the one number no analyst has been given a company anchor for. If the market had priced the denominator step-up and this management's demonstrated willingness to guide EPS down on integration costs, you would not see a -17.1 skew with calls bid, and previews would be leading on FY27 EPS rather than on NGS ARR and platformization. The 17 Feb 2026 episode is the proof of concept: a double beat, an EPS guide cut, -6.82% the next day.
findings.independence: That consensus equals guidance is independently established by the Hudson Labs preview dated 2026-08-10, which lists Q4 consensus of $3,352m / $0.97 / 830-840m shares: https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/palo-alto-networks-q4-2026-earnings-preview-panw-results-preview . The Feb 2026 guide cut and the reason for it are independently reported by CNBC, 2026-02-17: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/17/palo-alto-networks-panw-q2-2026-earnings.html . The -6.82% realised move is from the Yahoo bar series (163.50 close 17 Feb, 152.35 close 18 Feb): https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PANW?period1=1770940800&period2=1771632000&interval=1d - same price series flagged in finding 1.

findings.finding: PANW's GSA OneGov agreement gives every federal agency up to 60% off list on designated bundles of Prisma AIRS Runtime Security, VM-Series software firewalls, Panorama/CDSS, Prisma SASE and Prisma Browser (35% on Code to Cloud) through 31 Jan 2028 - and PANW's fiscal Q1 FY27, the quarter it guides tonight, is the first US federal year-end (30 Sep) buying quarter to run entirely under that pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: This is nine months old and on GSA's own newsroom, but it has never been connected to a guide: the federal year-end quarter is the volume quarter, and this is the first one where the price realisation on exactly the products PANW is marketing as its growth engine (Prisma AIRS, Prisma SASE) is capped 60% below list. If the market had priced it, the sell-side previews would carry a federal price-realisation line - the two previews I read (Hudson Labs 10 Aug, the 30 Aug Barchart/Yahoo piece) discuss only NGS ARR, RPO, platformization and organic growth, and neither mentions federal pricing at all. I size this small and with a band that nearly straddles zero because deep discounts in a year-end quarter can be volume-accretive, which is the honest ambiguity.
findings.independence: Independently reported by Nextgov/FCW with the December 2025 date in the URL path: https://www.nextgov.com/acquisition/2025/12/palo-alto-networks-offers-discounted-cybersecurity-solutions-agencies-through-onegov-deal/409923/ . Separate source, separate document from findings 1 and 2.

searched_and_found_nothing: 8-K filed 2026-08-21 (items 5.02/5.03, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327567/000119312526361122/d180372d8k.htm): looked like a governance tell 12 days before the print, but the substance is a standard double-trigger CIC severance policy (CEO 200% salary + 200% bonus, 24 months COBRA, 100% equity acceleration; others 150%) with NO officer departure, plus restated bylaws described as conforming to recent Delaware law changes. Read it as post-acquisition housekeeping for an enlarged executive bench, not a signal. Coverage limited to TipRanks/GuruFocus, which is consistent with it being routine.

Two actively-exploited critical PAN-OS zero-days landed in the first month of fiscal Q4: CVE-2026-0300 (CVSS 9.3 root RCE via the User-ID Captive Portal, disclosed 2026-05-06, https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/06/palo-alto-firewalls-vulnerability-exploited-cve-2026-0300/) and CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS 9.1 GlobalProtect auth bypass, CISA KEV 2026-05-29, https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/29/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog). Discarded as an edge: PANW reported Q3 on 2026-06-02 AFTER both were public and raised the Q4 guide, so management has already spoken to them.

CyberArk purchase-accounting distortion: the Q3 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001327567/000132756726000015/panw-20260430.htm) does not quantify a deferred-revenue fair-value haircut, and PANW already disclosed the inorganic revenue contribution outright ($388m in Q3), so there is no hidden wedge to exploit. The 'organic growth is bought not earned' angle was already published on 2026-08-30 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/investors-watch-buying-panw-stock-153002874.html).

The 112m-share CyberArk issuance diluting the EPS denominator vendor consensus is built on: dead end as a Q4 surprise, because consensus shares of 830-840m are identical to the company's guide. The residual risk is FY27 only, which is finding 2.

Israeli/TASE filings for a mooted secondary 'CYBR' listing: found nothing. CyberArk is now consolidated and rebranded 'Idira' (announced 2026-05-12, https://www.sdxcentral.com/news/palo-alto-networks-rebrands-cyberark-with-idira-platform-release/); no securities filing or listing document surfaced.

Competitor read-across for CyberArk churn: Okta's 26 Aug 2026 print (rev +11% to $805m, FY27 guide raised, stock +20%) and Fortinet's 29 Jul 2026 print (product rev +52%) show a booming market with no sign of anyone claiming PANW/CyberArk displacement wins. Read-across is positive, not negative, and is already in the tape.

Insider activity: no datable Form 4 cluster found for August 2026 beyond a routine in-kind transaction; the one search hit claiming a $10m CEO open-market purchase (intellectia.ai) carried no verifiable date and was dropped.
Customer-side sentiment: no PANW-specific reddit/community thread on pricing, renewal quotes or licensing surfaced; search returned unrelated Adobe threads. Absence, not evidence.

Explaining the 63% realised vol: fully accounted for by two identified jumps in the daily bars - a -5.2% slide from 357.87 (21 Aug) to 339.31 (26 Aug) and the +12.84% rumour pop on 27 Aug - so there is no unexplained repricing left to hunt.
baseline_tension: Mixed and I want to be explicit about it: the reaction history I rebuilt AGREES with the -17.1 calls-bid skew on the only subsample that matters tonight (PANW's two prior fiscal-year-end August prints were +7.19% and +3.06%, the only positives in seven), so I do not claim the skew is wrong in general - but all three of my findings cut against it, because the specific things that can go wrong tonight (an unanchored FY27 EPS guide on a ~10% larger share count, a live named deal rumour that the market has priced as a positive when PANW's own deal announcements have been sold, and capped federal price realisation into the guide quarter) are all downside events on a name where downside is the cheap side of the chain and the run-up has already been half-unwound today.
